newsitem.title: NIGERIA: U.N. postpones mission to Nigeria, Cameroon.
newsitem.headline: U.N. postpones mission to Nigeria, Cameroon.

text.p: The United Nations has postponed a mission to examine the dispute between Nigeria and Cameroon over the Bakassi peninsula in the oil-rich Gulf of Guinea, the national news agency said on Monday.
The News Agency of Nigeria quoted U.N. spokeswoman in New York, Sylvana Foa, as saying the mission would be delayed because its itinerary coincided with that of a Commonwealth delegation.

The mission, to be headed by Indonesian Omar Halim, was initially scheduled to leave New York on Friday, and would have involved consultations with both governments. It would also have visited the disputed area.
"We are waiting to hear from the Nigerian ambassador to the U.N. for a better date," Foa said.
Since February 1994, troops of both Nigeria and Cameroon have clashed over the Bakassi peninsula, a string of impoverished islands which may conceal significant oil reserves.
In March, the International Court of Justice at The Hague ordered the two sides to halt hostilities pending its final decision on who owns the peninsula.

A four man team from the Commonwealth of Britain and its former colonies arrived in the Nigerian capital, Abuja, on Monday for talks with government officials to try to agree conditions for a later visit by Commonwealth ministers concerned over human rights.
